comment: What each lane of scripts/verify.ps1 needs, so agentq can place it without knowing this repository. Lane names are the -Lane values. A toolchain names the image family devcloud-ci-<toolchain>, baked by E:\gh\vmui\infra\devcloud\images. Schema and validator: E:\gh\vmui\infra\devcloud\profile. Values here are facts, never secrets.

rust.why: The lane ends with the release performance budget (cargo test -p vitals-win --release --test overhead), which is a budget rather than a benchmark: another heavy job on the same VM moves the numbers and turns a healthy tree red. Measured 2026-11-24 on the gate driver: the same member ran 21.3 s idle and 129.9 s under load.

android.why: The Gradle daemon outlives its client and keeps the stdio it inherited open, which stopped two different readers from ever finishing on 2026-11-25: the job runner, which ended a step on a closed pipe and therefore never published an exit code, and the lane above the gate, which ended on the pipeline's EOF and returned 41 s after a gate that had finished in 0.2 s. Both now wait for a process; a second job in the same Gradle user home is also the documented way to corrupt incremental state.

linux.why: Two reasons, both hard: vitals-core must keep compiling where vitals-win does not exist, so the lane needs a Linux host even when the rest of the run is on Windows; and a cargo clippy over the whole workspace is the memory-heaviest member this repository has, so it does not go beside another job in the same tree.
